title: A Orchard for the Typewriter
premise: In 1917, on a storm-battered island off the Cornish coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Xanthe Thackeray records every ship, storm, and stranger in her late husband's typewriter log. When a sealed letter arrives naming her as heir to the Thackeray orchard estate — and to a family secret entangled with a wartime smuggling ring that moved both contraband and deserters — she must leave the light for the mainland. As the armistice negotiations stall, Xanthe races to document the truth of who betrayed whom before government historians bury it, discovering along the way that the ragtag household of keepers, farmers, and runaways she gathers is the family she never had. She ends the war not with the estate intact but with the record published, the orchard planted anew, and her name — chosen, not inherited — on the title page.
about_author: Jonah Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal shipping logs from the First World War. They write historical fiction about people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A winter gale tests the lamp; she polishes the lens her husband Elias maintained and types the night's log in his cadence. Establishes her ritual of measuring life in portable things. Emotional beat: grief worn as competence.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed Twice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A solicitor's letter arrives, sealed within an older envelope bearing her father-in-law's crest, naming her sole heir to Thackeray Orchard. She burns nothing and tells no one. Beat: suspicion blooming inside loneliness.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She inventories the lighthouse: the typewriter, two lenses' worth of spare parts, Elias's coat. The relief keeper, young Tom Wrenn, begs to come along. Beat: the first crack in her solitude.

chapters.title: The Road Inland
chapters.summary: Tom's POV. The journey to Cornwall's orchard country; Tom watches Xanthe flinch at every signpost with the name Thackeray. Beat: wonder curdling into unease at what inheritance costs.

chapters.title: An Orchard Gone Wild
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The estate is overgrown, half-ruined, and occupied — by three squatters: an elderly gardener named Prue, a deserter called Fen, and a mute boy, Ollie. Beat: hostility with an undertow of recognition.

chapters.title: Terms of Tenancy
chapters.summary: Prue's POV. Prue recounts serving the Thackerays for forty years and warns Xanthe that the last letter naming an heir was burned unread. Beat: loyalty tested against old wounds.

chapters.title: The Locked Potting Shed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She finds the shed padlocked with a keyhole shaped wrong for any key she owns; inside, something metallic catches moonlight through the boards. Beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Fen, hiding his desertion, helps Xanthe sort the estate office and notices pages razored from the shipping ledgers — years matching the great storms. Beat: two secrets circling each other.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Version
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The local vicar offers a polished family history that contradicts the ledgers; he presses her to donate the papers to a 'war memorial archive.' Beat: the sense that someone is writing history ahead of her.

chapters.title: Ollie Speaks
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV, sparse and childlike. The boy speaks for the first time, describing boats that came to the cove at night and men who never came back. Beat: innocence as testimony.

chapters.title: Smugglers or Saints
chapters.summary: Prue's POV. Prue admits the orchard's cellars sheltered deserters and moved wounded men inland — until someone informed, and a boat was lost with all hands, including Xanthe's father-in-law's brother. Beat: the family myth inverted.

chapters.title: The Typewriter as Witness
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She begins transcribing testimonies — Prue, Fen, Ollie — onto the typewriter, dating each page like a log entry. Beat: purpose kindling; the record becomes her mission.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A naval requisition claims the island lighthouse for decommissioning; everything she kept there will be carried away or scrapped. Beat: loss sharpening her resolve to keep what matters.

chapters.title: Tom Returns
chapters.summary: Tom's POV. Tom arrives with news: the vicar's memorial archive is funded by the Admiralty, and its historian is already collecting 'corrected' accounts. Beat: the race becomes real.

chapters.title: The Informer's Name
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Cross-referencing paybooks and letters, Fen narrows the informer to two names — one dead, one very much alive and now a county magistrate. Beat: dread; truth has powerful enemies.

chapters.title: Harvest Without Hands
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating brief POVs. The household harvests the wild apples together; Ollie laughs; Xanthe realizes she has stopped counting what can be carried. Beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Visit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Magistrate Halloway tours the estate with velvet courtesy, offering to 'manage' the papers and hinting at charges against harborers of deserters. Beat: menace in a drawing room.

chapters.title: What Fen Confessed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Fen admits he deserted after refusing an order tied to the same convoy the informer betrayed; his testimony could hang him. Beat: trust weighed against survival.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV. Ollie produces the potting shed key, hidden in a birdhouse his father made. Inside: crates of undelivered letters, a ship's bell, and the true ledger. Beat: the past unlocked.

chapters.title: Reading by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Through the night she reads the true ledger — names of the drowned, payments received, Halloway's signature. She types a certified copy. Beat: cold clarity; the record is complete but dangerous.

chapters.title: Fire Watch
chapters.summary: Prue's POV. An unexplained fire guts the estate office; only the shed's contents, moved days earlier, survive. No one says arson aloud. Beat: fear binding the household tighter.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: Tom's POV. News travels that peace terms may be signed within weeks; afterward, official histories will harden like concrete. Their window is closing. Beat: urgency without panic yet.

chapters.title: Halloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Halloway proposes quietly: surrender the ledger, receive a pension and a clean name for the Thackerays. He invokes Elias's memory. Beat: temptation aimed at her loneliest nerve.

chapters.title: Elias's Letters
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Among the undelivered post she finds letters Elias wrote to his estranged father — proof Elias knew the family shame and chose the light anyway. Beat: grief transmuted into kinship across death.

chapters.title: The Household Votes
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Prue framing it. Around the kitchen table they vote: publish, whatever the cost. Fen abstains, then raises his hand. Beat: solidarity forged in risk.

chapters.title: Journey to the Port Town
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Fen and Xanthe travel to find a printer willing to set the document; most refuse under Halloway's shadow. One radical widow agrees. Beat: allies are scarce and precious.

chapters.title: The Historian's Visit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The Admiralty historian arrives, courteous and thorough, and reveals he suspects the official account is false but needs corroboration he can defend. Beat: an unexpected door opening.

chapters.title: Testimony on the Record
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She gives sworn-style deposition copies to the historian and the widow-printer simultaneously — duplication as insurance. Beat: strategy replacing fear.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Cove
chapters.summary: Tom's POV. Halloway's men raid the cove looking for Fen; Tom draws them off and is badly beaten. Beat: the cost becomes flesh and blood.

chapters.title: Vigil
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Ollie opening. The household keeps watch over Tom through the night; Prue tells stories of every person the orchard ever saved. Beat: tenderness at the edge of despair.

chapters.title: Warrant for Thackeray
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A warrant names Xanthe for harboring a deserter. She sends the ledger copy away with the widow and prepares to stand trial rather than flee. Beat: resolve hardened into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Courtroom Orchard
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the hearing, Prue, Ollie, and the historian testify; Fen surrenders himself voluntarily, gambling on the record. Beat: climax begins — truth versus authority in open court.

chapters.title: The Ledger Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The historian enters the true ledger into evidence; Halloway's signature, read aloud, breaks the room. The magistrate's patronage evaporates. Beat: catharsis — the victors' version collapses.

chapters.title: Armistice Day
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Xanthe closing. Bells ring out as the armistice is signed; the village celebrates awkwardly around the household that stood trial. Beat: public history and private grief colliding.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Fen receives a suspended sentence and a discharge paper; the historian's report forces review of the lost boat's crew. Beat: justice partial but real.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Prue's POV. Winter turns; the household prunes and replants the orchard rows with Elias's letters as planting markers. Beat: inheritance redefined as stewardship.

chapters.title: The Light Rekindled
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The decommissioned lighthouse is granted to her as a private beacon; she and Tom reinstall the lens. Beat: homecoming without retreat.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The printed account appears — not the Admiralty's, but hers, typed and sworn, sold cheaply in the port town. She signs it 'Xanthe Thackeray, keeper.' Beat: identity claimed.

chapters.title: First Blossom
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, final entry styled as a log. Spring: the first grafts blossom; Ollie reads aloud from the printed book; the household gathers under the trees. Beat: quiet, earned peace — the orchard keeps them all.
